newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., judge throws out stadium lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., judge throws out stadium lawsuit.

text.p: A Florida judge dismissed a lawsuit Friday that had threatened Hillsborough County bond financing for a $168 million football stadium for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Circuit Judge Sam Pendino dismissed the lawsuit with prejudice, which prevents the plaintiff, former Mayor William, from re-filing the lawsuit.
However, Poe has 30 days from the day the final order is entered to file an appeal.
County attorney Emily Acton said that the order would probably be filed by the end of next week, and the bonds would be sold as soon as the appeals period ends.
"We could be talking about the second week in November or very close to that," Acton said.
The bonds are to be issued by the Tampa Sports Authority via Smith Barney Inc.

The suit was the second filed by Poe to block the use of public funds to build a new stadium for the Bucs. Poe sued unsuccessfully in August to halt a referendum on the sales tax increase that will back the bonds. The effort failed when Hillsborough Circui Judge James Whittmore upheld the constitutionality of hte blalot question.
On Sept 3, voters approved the half-cent slaes tax increase that will raise $2.7 billion over 30 years for shools roads, public safety and the stadium.

Poe sued the county again last week, saying Whittmore had been legally barred from considering the stadium issue separately from the other projects to be funded with the tax money. He said the project would unconstitutionally use public money to benefit the private, for-profit football team.
Pendino dismissed the lawsuit Friday, agreeing with the county's argument that the suit raied the same issues that had already been litigated.
"He said it was the exact same thing," Acton said.
